cases.message: the declaration nests too deeply (more than 256 levels): flatten the nesting into separate fields or concepts
cases.note: The parser is recursive descent, and a goroutine stack overflow is a fatal error no recover() sees, so how deep it reads is bounded in every grammar it holds. The remedy is the DECLARATION one: "name its parts as separate statements" is the wrong instruction for a property or a container type. The depth at which an unbounded parse fails is a property of the stack ceiling rather than of the source's size, which is why no byte cap stands in for this.

A concept that does not parse is refused. At boot the concept loader parses each concept on its own and used to drop one that failed with nothing reported, so a node booted without it; it is a skip strict boot refuses now, concept_unparsed (memql#5426). The corpus reads the file with the parser every loader uses, which refuses it here.

A concept whose `{` never closes is refused. The corpus reads the whole file with the parser, which reads the next concept as a field of this one; the concept loader slices each concept on its own, and used to lose this one AND every concept below it without a word, because the unclosed brace left the rest of the file inside it. It refuses this one by name now, concept_unparsed, and builds the note below it (memql#5426).
